title: SHOOTING IN CENTRALIA
full_story:
Sunday afternoon a shooting was reported in the 900 block of East Kell Street in Centralia.  Available reports indicate that there was one death and at least three injuries.

Marion County Coroner Claude Howell confirms he was called to St. Mary’s Hospital in Centralia, where he pronounced one of the shooting victims dead.  The Illinois State Police has taken over the investigation.

Police agencies from the four-county area around Centralia were called to assist with the investigation, as well as to help with crowd control, which was an issue after the shooting occurred.

St. Mary’s Hospital was also reportedly locked down after the shooting victims were brought there.

State Police and Centralia Police have not released any other details at this time.

title: CLAY COUNTY MOBILE HOME TAXES
full_story:
The 2026 Mobile Home Privilege Tax Bills are being mailed out today.  The due date for mobile home taxes will be July 1st, but you can pay the taxes at any time.  After July 1st, you will be charged an additional $25.00 per month.

If you do not receive a mobile home Privilege tax bill, and you own a mobile home, please contact the Treasurer’s office immediately at 618-665-3727 or email [email protected].  That will give the office time to investigate the matter before it is at risk of becoming delinquent.

Clay County taxpayers can pay their mobile home taxes by mail by sending their check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.  Mobile home privilege tax bills can be paid at the Treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse, they accept cash, check, cashier’s check, or money orders.  Please bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  The Clay County Treasurer’s office hours are from 8 am to 4 pm and they are open during the noon hour.  Payment can be made by placing payment in the envelope depository at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.  Tax Bills can also be paid online by credit/debit card by going to govpaynow.com PLC number a00082.

title: PROM
full_story:

The promenade lineup will start at 6:30 pm on West North Avenue between Galaxie Gaming and Ace Hardware.  Vehicles will take a right on 3rd Street to Thomas Street, turn right and then left into the New Beginnings Church parking lot where students will unload and be announced in front of the main entrance.

Anyone wanting to watch the promenade may bring a lawn chair and watch from the designated viewing area in the parking lot.  Following Promenade, the Senior Court family with tickets may enter at 7 pm.  All other spectators can enter after Promenade.

title: NORTH CLAY BOARD
full_story:
The North Clay school board took action on several personnel matters at their monthly meeting on Wednesday.

The Board named Josh Zink as the girls varsity basketball coach.  Zink had coached Boys Varsity Basketball.  Allie Krutsinger was hired as girls basketball assistant coach; Allison Czyzewski was hired as girls basketball assistant coach; Kim Adair was approved as a girls basketball volunteer coach.  Lorissa Wolf was named high school head cheer coach, and Malorie Craig was named high school head volleyball coach.  Barry Adair was approved as junior high girls basketball volunteer assistant coach; and Brian Swope was approved as junior high track volunteer assistant coach.

In other business, the North Clay board expelled a student for the remainder of this school year and all of the 26-27 school year.  However, the expulsion will be held in abeyance if the student successfully completes a probation.

Jon Carroll with Poettker Construction presented bid results for upcoming summer projects.  The Board awarded the base bids that include a redesigned and expanded Pre-K playground, and an abatement of asbestos tile from high school classrooms.

The Board approved a bus bid from Central States, but did not accept a fuel bid, however they did authorize Superintendent Keith Price to lock in a price in the future.

Registration for the coming school year will take place online from July 19th through the 26th, with in-person registration day on Wednesday, July 22nd.

The Board set the fee schedule, set rates for officials pay and, renewed membership in the IESA.

title: OCC SPRING CONCERT
full_story:
The Olney Central College Music Department will present its Spring Concert at 7 pm on Wednesday, April 22nd in the Dr. John D. Stull Performing Arts Center.

The evening will feature performances by the OCC Community Concert Band and Jazz Combo, under the direction of OCC Interim Director of Bands Jena Combs.  Joining them as a special guest will be the Flora High School Band, directed by OCC alumnus Ethan Steber.

Combs is excited to include the high school students in the event, an idea that grew out of a conversation with Steber.

“We were talking about ways to get the community more involved, and the idea came up to invite high school bands to perform with us and feature them in a concert,” she said.  “Ethan immediately volunteered his band to be the first.  We thought it was a cool way to get people here and a great way to help with recruitment.”

Combs previously served as FHS band director before accepting a position at Lincoln Trail College in 2024 and assisting with OCC’s instrumental program this year.  Steber completed his student teaching under Combs and later succeeded her as Flora band director.

The FHS band will present The Great Rubber Chicken Galop by Randall Standridge, American Riversongs by Pierre LaPlante and The Pines of Rome by Ottorino Respighi and arranged by James Curnow.

The high school students will then have an opportunity to perform with the OCC Community Concert Band and the OCC Jazz Combo as the three ensembles come together for the selection Shine on Me by Seattle-based composer and conductor Erin Keeton-Howard.

The OCC Community Concert Band, which brings together OCC students and area musicians, will perform Prestissimo by march-music composer Karl L. King with the arrangement by James Swearingen, Secret Valley by Michael Sweeney and Amazing Grace by Frank Ticheli, whose many works have become standards in concert band repertoire.  Other pieces will include Nevermore and Reverberations by contemporary American composer, conductor and music educator Brian Balmages and Insurrection by composer Gary P. Gilroy.

Selections by the OCC Jazz Combo will include C Jam Blues by legendary jazz performer Duke Ellington and Someone to Watch Over Me by groundbreaking American composer and pianist George Gershwin.  Other pieces include Sonnymoon for Two by jazz saxophonist Sonny Rollins, Brasilian Skies by Masayoshi Takanaka and the Latin-rock hit Oye Como Va by Santana.

Combs invites the community to come out and enjoy this final instrumental performance of the semester.  Admission is a free-will donation.

title: BLOOD DRIVE
full_story:
With a Blood Emergency in place throughout the Midwest, the American Red Cross is asking area blood donors to get out and give blood at their next earliest opportunity.

In response to the critical need for blood, the American Red Cross will have a blood drive tomorrow from 3 to 7 pm at the Floyd Henson JR High.  There are currently only 3 appointments available for Power Red donors.  There are a number of Blood Drive appointments available and walk ins will be welcome.

Donors, especially those with type O blood and those giving platelets, can help bolster the blood supply now by making an appointment to give in the coming weeks.  Make an appointment to donate by downloading the free Red Cross Blood Donor App, visiting redcrossblood.org or calling 1-800-RED CROSS (1-800-733-2767).  A donor card, driver’s license, or two forms of ID are required at check-in.

Those who give blood or platelets at this drive will get a $15 e-gift card to the merchant of their choice.

After tomorrow’s drive the next Blood drives in our area will be on Tuesday April 28th at the Flora High School from 8:30 am till 2 pm.  There are currently 10 Power Red Blood donation appointments available at this drive.

title: HBO FILMING IN FAIRFIELD
full_story:
Filming is set to begin at the end of the week for an HBO Max show about the 2014 murder of Fairfield teen Megan Nichols.  The 15-year-old Fairfield High School student died at the hands of her boyfriend at the time, Brodey Murbarger, who is currently serving a 50-year prison sentence.

The Megan Nichols story will be an episode of “A Killer Among Friends,” an HBO Max true crime series narrated by Jennifer Love Hewitt.

The film will be shot entirely in Fairfield and will feature interviews with family members and friends of Megan, as well as others involved in the reporting, investigation and eventual prosecution of Brodey Murbarger.

Producers in Los Angeles and New York have been researching the case and scheduling interviews for the show over the past four months.  The series delves into the lives of interconnected individuals who were deeply affected by the murder of one of their own.

Nichols, went missing from her home in Fairfield July 3rd, 2014.  Her remains were found December 26th of 2017.  A short time after the body was positively identified, Fairfield native Brodey I. Murbarger of Evansville was arrested and charged with first-degree murder.

Officials stated Megan’s cause of death was probable asphyxiation by homicidal violence.  A jury convicted Murbarger following an October, 2022 trial.
